footer.about: Creekmore Plumbing is a third generation, family owned and operated plumbing business at 440 South Pattie Street in Wichita. We repair and replace water heaters and toilets, work on water lines, test backflow devices and fit water softeners.

why: Your site is two pages, with every service in one long column. The headline, “Reliable local plumbers you can trust,” doesn't say Wichita or name a service, so Google can't tell what you want to be found for.

Your site shows no reviews: “See What Our Customers Are Saying About Creekmore Plumbing!” sits over a blank space. On Google, Richard W. wrote that “it is family owned and has been around Wichita for years.”

So the demo tells one story: a third generation family plumber who explains the problem in plain words. It opens with plumber in Wichita, KS, and gives water heater replacement and toilet repair a page each.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe the company you are. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we’ll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site says you've served the community since 1948, while a Better Business Bureau listing we saw shows 1962, so which year should every listing use?
Google lists you as “Creekmore Plumbing-Heating Inc,” while your website says only “Creekmore Plumbing” and lists no heating, so which name and which services should every listing use?
Your header and contact block use creekmoreph@att.net, while your Get a Free Estimate button uses stevecoleman@creekmoreplumbing.com, so which email should every listing use?

lead.heading: Why we led with the family plumber, honest fix first
lead.text: A page that says what every plumber says gives Google nothing to rank, so we built this one on things it can't find anywhere else. Your site says third generation, and your Google reviews add Jane K.'s three grown sons and Donna R.'s parents' house and rentals, all in your customers' own words. Your site says it, so tell us if we have the family story right.

unverified.heading: What we couldn't verify, and why it matters
unverified.intro: We marked these on the demo as yellow "to confirm" tags instead of guessing, because we won't put a claim on your site we can't back up. Your current site has no license number, no warranty terms and no list of towns.

items.why: A family handing you their parents' house, then their own, wants to be able to look the license up before the plumber comes through the door.
Your site states no warranty, and someone paying for a water heater will ask what happens if it fails.
"Wichita" alone doesn't tell a family in the next town over whether you'll come.

unverified.closing: This is what our onboarding call nails down. Fifteen minutes, and every tag becomes a real, true line.
